data.title: Indian rupee rises past 93/USD as portfolio inflows, bear retreat fuel rally
data.description:
The Indian rupee strengthened past the psychologically important 93-per-dollar mark for the first time since April on Friday, as robust foreign portfolio inflows and trimming of bearish bets boosted the South Asian unit.

The rupee (INR=In) rose to a peak of 92.9950 per dollar, up 0.3% from its closing level in the previous session and 2% for the month so far.

Overseas investors have poured more than $12 billion into Indian stocks so far in November.

The inflows have helped the rupee outperform all its Asian peers this month. Regional currencies have come under pressure from a broadly firmer dollar amid growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will pursue a more hawkish rate path than previously anticipated.

data.title: Everest Medicines Announces First Patient Dosed in ASCEND Phase 2b Trial of VIS-101 in Wet AMD
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Everest Medicines (HKEX 1952.HK, "Everest", or the "Company"), a biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, clinical development, manufacturing and commercialization of innovative therapeutics, announced that the first patient has been treated in the ASCEND study, a randomized Phase 2b trial evaluating two doses of VIS-101 (6 mg and 9 mg) head-to-head against 2 mg aflibercept in approximately 244 treatment-naïve patients with wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD). The study is being conducted in China in partnership with Visara, Inc., a majority-owned ophthalmology subsidiary of NovaBridge Biosciences, Inc. ().

ASCEND's primary efficacy endpoint is the change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) from baseline to Week 36 versus aflibercept dosed every eight weeks. The goal of the ASCEND study is to determine the dose(s) to advance into VIS-101's global Phase 3 program based on safety, efficacy and durability.

VIS-101 is a purpose-designed tetravalent, dual VEGF-A x ANG-2 inhibitor in development for retinal vascular diseases, including wet AMD, diabetic macular edema (DME) and retinal vein occlusion (RVO). In the randomized, dose ranging Phase 2a study, VIS-101 demonstrated rapid, robust, and durable treatment responses in wet AMD, along with a favorable safety profile. Approximately 50% of patients in the 6 mg treatment-naïve cohort remained retreatment-free six months after the last loading dose.

Wet AMD affects more than 20 million people globally[1]. In China, the prevalent patient population of AMD and DME exceeds 15 million, with around 600,000 new cases each year, yet only about 500,000 patients currently receive treatment.

"Patients with wet AMD and other retinal vascular diseases have significant unmet needs, as treatment burden remains a meaningful challenge for both patients and physicians," said Rogers Yongqing Luo, Chief Executive Officer of Everest Medicines. "Dosing the first patient in the Phase 2b ASCEND study marks an important step in the clinical development of VIS-101. With encouraging efficacy, safety and durability results observed in Phase 2a, we believe VIS-101 has the potential to offer longer intervals between injections and sustained disease control. ASCEND will further evaluate this potential against an established standard of care, with findings supporting future global development.

Our established clinical and commercial capabilities across China and other Asian markets will enable us to accelerate efforts to bring VIS-101 to patients and make this innovative therapy available to more patients."

On October 30, 2025, Everest Medicines entered into a collaboration agreement with Visara, under which Everest acquired an exclusive license to develop, manufacture, and commercialize VIS-101 in Greater China, Singapore, South Korea, and certain Southeast Asian countries.

About the ASCEND Phase 2b Trial

ASCEND is a randomized, quadruple-masked, active-controlled, head-to-head Phase 2b study (NCT07798375) to evaluate the safety and efficacy of VIS-101 (aka AM712 or ASKG712) in approximately 244 treatment naïve patients with wet AMD in China. Patients will be randomized to either 6 mg or 9 mg VIS-101, or 2 mg aflibercept, a standard-of-care anti-VEGF therapy. All patients will initially receive three monthly doses of either VIS-101 or aflibercept and can then be retreated based on protocol-specified retreatment criteria that are the same for all groups up to Month 9. The main objectives are to determine the dose(s) to be studied in Phase 3 clinical trials and establish the initial durability with treatment intervals up to seven months after three loading doses.

About VIS-101

VIS-101 (also known as ASKG712 or AM712), is a dual VEGF-A X ANG-2 inhibitor in development for the treatment of retinal vascular diseases, such as wet AMD, diabetic macular edema (DME) and retinal vein occlusion (RVO). VIS-101's bispecific, tetravalent design format provides more binding sites and increased VEGF-A and ANG-2 affinity and avidity, for rapid, robust and durable responses. VIS-101 has completed initial safety and dose-escalation studies in both the US and China and a randomized, dose-ranging 2a study in China (NCT05456828). VIS-101 is currently being evaluated in the dose-determining Phase 2b ASCEND study, with initiation of the global Phase 3 program planned as early as 2027.

About Everest Medicines

Everest Medicines is a biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing, manufacturing and commercializing innovative pharmaceutical products that address critical unmet medical needs for patients in global markets. The management team of Everest Medicines has deep expertise and an extensive track record both in China and with leading global pharmaceutical companies. The Company owns a global manufacturing base of commercial scale in Jiashan, Zhejiang Province, and has established a comprehensive GMP production quality management system in accordance with China, EU, and WHO standards.

The Company's therapeutic areas of focus include autoimmune, ophthalmology, critical care, and CKM (cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic) diseases. Everest Medicines has developed a fully integrated commercialization platform that combines omnichannel commercial capabilities with end-to-end product lifecycle management. Its pharmaceutical distribution capabilities further complement its existing manufacturing and commercialization operations, supporting efficient product supply and delivery to the market.

Leveraging its proprietary mRNA platform, the Company is advancing its existing pipeline, including mRNA in vivo CAR-T and mRNA cancer vaccines, while selectively expanding into additional high-value therapeutic areas with blockbuster potential, and accelerating its global expansion.

For more information, please visit the Company's website: www.everestmedicines.com.

data.title: China's refined copper imports set to jump in 2027, traders and analysts say
data.description:
Key points:
  • China's refined copper output likely to flatten next year, analysts say
  • China's copper demand to grow by 4% in 2027, says CRU
  • Chile's Codelco offering Chinese customers lower premiums
  • US copper tariffs remain uncertain

By Amy Lv and Tony Munroe

China's imports of refined copper are poised to climb in 2027 following this year's rare drop, as persistent feedstock shortages curb domestic supply even as demand continues to rise, according to 15 industry analysts and traders polled by Reuters.

Higher imports will help the world's top consumer of the red metal used in construction, power grids and electric vehicles to regain some of the pricing power that has shifted to the United States.

"China will have to import more refined copper next year because its refined production growth will remain very limited, constrained by persistently tight concentrate supply," said Nicholas Snowdon, head of metals and mining research at Mercuria, on the sidelines of this week's World Copper Conference Asia.

SLOWING DOMESTIC SUPPLY

China's refined copper output this year is projected to grow at its slowest pace in decades, hampered by a prolonged concentrate shortage and reduced availability of scrap copper amid stricter enforcement of tax and invoicing policy.

Slowing supply growth and rapid inventory drawdowns have led to acute tightness in physical copper in China, where soaring spot premiums have compelled some traders to rush to import refined copper, including from the US.

"The gravitational pull of refined copper is now towards China, which has regained at least for now the pricing power that the US has dominated in the last two years," said Snowdon.

However, Raghav Jain, head of copper pricing at information provider Argus, expects a moderate recovery rather than a surge from the unusual weakness in 2026.

"We expect some normalisation of global cathode flows back towards China in 2027 if the US arbitrage remains less attractive," said Jain.

China's refined copper imports in the first 10 months of 2026 slid by 16% from the same time last year to 2.37 million tons, their lowest for the period since at least 2015, keeping total inbound shipments on track for an annual decline.

RISING COPPER CONSUMPTION

While tepid construction activity remains a drag, China's copper demand will grow by 4% in 2027 following this year's 2% increase, He Tianyu, analyst at consultancy CRU Group, told delegates on Wednesday.

"China's overall copper demand will keep rising over the next five years, but the structure is shifting with new growth drivers," said He, who expects the combined demand from power grids, data centres, renewables, energy storage and electric vehicles to make up 59% of the consumption increase in that period.

Chile's Codelco is offering refined copper to Chinese customers in 2027 at lower premiums than those charged this year to revive its sales in the world's biggest metals market.

US TARIFF UNCERTAINTY

However, US tariff policies remain uncertain.

Expectations for US tariffs on copper imports have upended global flows, with bumper US premiums over London Metal Exchange benchmark prices sucking in vast amounts of copper over the past two years, creating tightness elsewhere.

Washington has proposed a 15% tariff on refined copper imports starting in 2027, but it remains unclear whether such a duty will ultimately be implemented.

"The US midterm election result does not remove the US president's Section 232 authority, so tariff uncertainty has diminished rather than disappeared," said Argus' Jain.

data.title: Gold, silver ETFs crash up to 7.5% as bullion prices plunge; gold heads for biggest weekly fall since March
data.description:
Gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) plunged up to 7.5 percent on Friday as international bullion prices extended their sharp selloff amid expectations of further interest-rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve. Silver ETFs suffered the steepest losses, while gold ETFs declined more than 5 percent, tracking a global precious metals rout that has pushed gold prices to their lowest level in over a year.

Nippon India Silver ETF (SILVERBEES) was among the biggest losers, plunging 7.47 percent to Rs 141.39. SBI Silver ETF declined 7.39 percent to Rs 145.15, while Tata Silver ETF fell 7.32 percent to Rs 14.44. ICICI Prudential Silver ETF also lost 7.29 percent to trade at Rs 147.57.

Gold ETFs witnessed similarly sharp selling pressure. ICICI Prudential Gold ETF (GOLDIETF) tumbled 5.69 percent to Rs 103.86, while Nippon India ETF Gold BeES (GOLDBEES) declined 5.59 percent to Rs 100.36. Tata Gold ETF slipped 5.43 percent to Rs 11.85, while SBI Gold ETF was down 5.4 percent at Rs 103.4.

The sharp decline in precious metal ETFs came even as the broader equity market traded largely unchanged. At 10:08 am, the Sensex was up 234 points, or 0.03 percent, at 83,045.7, while the Nifty gained 9 points to 25,523.4.

  • Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty today

Gold heads for biggest weekly decline since March

International gold prices fell for a fifth consecutive session on Friday, heading for their steepest weekly decline since March as hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve and a selloff in artificial intelligence-related stocks intensified pressure on bullion.

Spot gold dropped 2.3 percent to $3,543.19 per ounce at 10:15 am in Singapore, after falling as much as 2.4 percent earlier in the session to below $3,540. The metal is on track to lose nearly 9 percent this week, having slipped to its lowest level since September 2025.

Silver also extended its decline, falling 2.3 percent to $41.98 per ounce after plunging nearly 5 percent in the previous session. The metal has lost around 14 percent during the week.

The selloff has been driven by expectations of further US interest-rate hikes as the Federal Reserve maintains a hawkish stance amid persistent inflation. Higher interest rates and bond yields typically weigh on gold by increasing the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding metal.

Bullion has also faced selling pressure amid a rout in technology and AI-related stocks, prompting some investors to liquidate gold holdings to cover losses elsewhere.

Gold has now fallen by approximately a third since the US-Iran war began in late February, as higher energy costs fuelled inflation and strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy.

MCX gold, silver futures extend sharp losses

Domestic precious metal futures also witnessed heavy selling on Friday. MCX gold futures for December delivery opened 3.94 percent lower at Rs 1,22,430 per 10 grams, while silver futures plunged 5.73 percent to Rs 1,48,466 per kg in early trade. The latest decline followed Thursday's closing levels of Rs 1,29,380 per 10 grams for gold and Rs 1,61,166 per kg for silver in the domestic market.

data.title: Advanced Enzyme raises JC Biotech stake in India
data.description:
Indian enzyme maker Advanced Enzyme Technologies (BSE: 540025) has bought another 1.22% of its subsidiary JC Biotech Private Limited, raising its holding to 96.94%, the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 19.

The stake had previously stood at 95.72%. The purchase moves the Mumbai-listed group closer to owning the unit outright. The company is working to acquire the outstanding 3.06% of JC Biotech, which would then become a wholly owned subsidiary.

Advanced Enzyme paid INR22.80mn ($244,838) for 253,297 equity shares, bought from a small number of JC Biotech's existing shareholders. That works out to INR90 per share. The higher ownership level took effect on November 18 and is measured against JC Biotech's paid-up share capital, the filing said.

The company first told the exchanges about the planned purchase in a notice dated August 8. The latest filing confirms the deal has been completed. It does not give a price or a timetable for buying the remaining shares. The disclosure was signed by Sanjay Basantani, company secretary and head of legal at Advanced Enzyme Technologies. It was sent to both the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India.

data.title: GTA-VI Launch: A look at how the Sensex has performed across every Grand Theft Auto era
data.description:
The Grand Theft Auto (GTA-VI) has finally launched after a wait of more than a decade. For three decades, every major releases in the GTA franchise has coincided with some of the most defining moments in global financial history. From currency crises and dot-com booms to financial meltdowns and AI-driven market shifts, each gaming era tells a distinct story for Indian equities. Here's a look back at this journey from 1997 till date.

GTA Launch & The Asian Financial Crisis of 1997 | The GTA franchise debuted just as financial turmoil erupted across Asia, starting in Thailand in July 1997. Rapid currency depreciation and mounting concerns over banking sector stability sent shockwaves through emerging markets. Despite a steep intra-year correction of 27%, the Sensex showed resilience and closed 1997 with a 13% gain, courtesy of the then "dream budget". However, the delayed fallout hit Indian equities harder in 1998, dragging the index down by 17%.

GTA II, Post-Crisis Recovery & The Dot-Com Boom | By the time GTA 2 hit shelves, Asian economies were firmly on the path to recovery from the 1997–98 crisis. Simultaneously, global technology stocks were surging at the height of the dot-com boom, lifting investor sentiment worldwide. Fuelled by economic recovery and tech optimism, the Sensex delivered a stellar 64% return in 1999.

GTA III, Dot-Com Bust & The Geopolitical Shock | GTA III revolutionized open-world gaming during a year of severe global economic distress. Following the Nasdaq’s peak in March 2000, the dot-com bubble had burst, wiping out trillions in tech valuations. The September 11 terrorist attacks further compounded global uncertainty. Indian equities also faced heavy selling pressure. The Sensex suffered a intra-year drawdown of roughly 41% before ending 2001 with losses of 18%.

GTA IV & The Global Financial Crisis of 2008 | Liberty City returned at the epicenter of the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression. The collapse of the US subprime mortgage market—culminating in the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers in September 2008, triggered a worldwide liquidity freeze and recession fears. Global equities plunged, and India was no exception. The Sensex experienced one of its worst calendar years on record, tanking 51% in 2008.

GTA V, European Debt & The Taper Tantrum | When GTA V launched, the acute phase of the European debt crisis had passed, though its shadow still lingered over global growth. Closer to home, emerging markets were rattled when the US Federal Reserve signaled plans to scale back bond purchases, sparking the "Taper Tantrum" and causing the Indian Rupee to weaken sharply. Volatility returned to Indian equities, with the Sensex enduring a 12% intra-year correction. Ultimately, the market shook off the currency jitters to finish the year with gains of 8%.

GTA VI Arrives Amidst The AI Valuation Reset | After a 13-year hiatus, GTA-VI enters a vastly transformed financial landscape. Today’s markets are defined by a critical inflection point in global technology. Investors are actively scrutinizing stretched technology multiples against actual earnings delivery. After years of relentless momentum, the global artificial intelligence trade is witnessing heightened volatility as capital rotates and market participants separate long-term winners from hype.

data.title: Tips Films shares hit 20% upper circuit on voluntary delisting plan; promoters to acquire 25% public stake – what it means for existing shareholders
data.description:
Shares of Tips Films Ltd surged 20 percent to hit the upper circuit at Rs 434.70 in early trade on Friday, November 20, after the company announced a voluntary delisting proposal under which its promoters intend to acquire the remaining public shareholders and take the company private.

Tips Films share price today

Tip Films shares opened at Rs 394.80 on the BSE and rallied 20 percent to hit the upper circuit at Rs 434.70. The stock closed at Rs 394.80 the previous day. At around 10 am, the stock was trading at Rs 430, up 18.70 percent.

Tips Films Limited, in a regulatory filing shared during the market hours on Thursday, announced that it has received an Initial Public Announcement (IPA) from its promoters expressing their intention to voluntarily delist the company's equity shares from the stock exchanges.

The disclosure was made on behalf of the acquirers by Inga Ventures Pvt. Ltd., which is acting as the manager to the offer under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) delisting regulations.

Tips Films delisting proposal

Under the delisting proposal, initiated by the two promoters of the company - Kumar S Taurani and Ramesh S Taurani, intend to purchase all the equity shares held by public shareholders, either individually or collectively. Once the delisting is completed, the shares of Tip Films would no longer trade on either BSE or NSE.

What is delisting of shares?

For the unversed, delisting involves removal of listed securities of a company from a stock exchange where it is traded on a permanent basis. It can be done either on voluntary decision of the company or forcibly done by SEBI on account of some wrong doing by the company.

Tips Films delisting: What does the proposal include?

The voluntary delisting proposal covers 10,81,770 fully paid-up equity shares of Tips Films, each with a face value of Rs 10. The shares represent 25.02 percent of the company's total paid-up equity capital held by public shareholders.

Promoters held a 74.98 percent stake in the company at the end of the September quarter. Kumar and Ramesh Taurani individually hold a combined stake of 40.5 percent, while the remaining promoter shareholding is held by other members of the promoter group and entities.

Why are the promoters proposing to delist Tips Films?

The main objective of the delisting proposal is to obtain full ownership of the company by the acquirers along with other members of the promoter group which will in turn provide increased operational, financial and strategic flexibility for, including but not limited to, supporting the company's business, undertaking corporate restructurings or acquisitions, exploring new financing structures including financial support from the members of the promoter group and making investments in the company, said Tips Films in the regulatory filing, explaining the rationale behind the delisting proposal.

Additionally, the delisting proposal will result in reduction of the ongoing substantial compliance costs and dedicated management time being incurred associated with continued listing of equity shares, which can be refocused on its business, the filing said.

Lastly, the offer provides public shareholders an opportunity to realise immediate liquidity and a certain value for their equity shares amid elevated market volatility, priced according to SEBI delisting regulations, the company said.

Tip Films delisting: Floor price, other details

The delisting price will be determined in accordance with SEBI's prescribed framework for calculating the floor price and the final delisting price.

“We will separately inform the “Floor Price” and the “Fixed Delisting Price” in accordance with the aforesaid provisions, in due course,” said the company in the filing.

Tip Films delisting conditions

The proposal is subject to several regulatory and shareholder approval requirements and is not final yet. The acquisition of equity shares by the acquirers with other members of the promoter group, from the public shareholders will be conditional upon the following:

  • Completion of due diligence by a peer reviewed company secretary as required under a norm of delisting regulations.
  • The Board approving the delisting proposal in accordance with a regulation of the delisting regulations.
  • The approval of the shareholders of the company by way of a special resolution in accordance with a norm of the Delisting Regulations and other applicable law wherein the number of votes cast by the public shareholders in favour of the delisting proposal is at least two times the number of votes cast by the public shareholders against it.
  • In addition, the company will need to secure approvals from the stock exchanges and any other statutory, regulatory or third-party approvals, wherever required.
  • The delisting will also depend on the shares being tendered meeting the prescribed threshold under SEBI regulations, along with other conditions outlined in the upcoming Detailed Public Announcement, Letter of Offer and related disclosures.

Tips Film share price history

Tips Films shares witnessed a sharp spike towards the close of Thursday's trading session following the delisting announcement. The stock ended the session 7.2 percent lower at Rs 392, however, the stock is up just 1 percent so far this year.

In the past three months, the stock has gained 20.69 percent and in six months, it has rises 14.35 percent and in one year, it rallied by 8.43 percent.

data.title: Gold, Silver Drop to Lowest Levels in Over a Year
data.description:
By Megan Cheah

Gold and silver fell to their lowest levels in over a year as the precious metals were weighed by growing expectations higher interest rates globally.

Expectations for tighter monetary policy appear to have overshadowed the typical demand for the yellow metal as a safe haven for risk-averse investors. That's notable as the precious metals are weakening despite heavy losses for Asian stock markets on Friday.

Spot prices for gold dropped to a low of $3,517.44 a troy ounce in Asian trade, ICE data showed. Spot silver hit a low of $41.20 an ounce. Both are at levels last seen in September 2025.

Gold was last 2.8% lower at $3,522.08 an ounce while silver was down 3.5% at $41.36 an ounce.

Japan's consumer inflation data for October released Friday showed prices were accelerating past the Bank of Japan's target. That reinforced expectations for tighter policy as policymakers grow increasingly worried about the risk of higher prices due to increased energy costs, persistent yen weakness and rising semiconductor prices amid the artificial-intelligence boom.

"A rate hike at the next meeting in December looks highly likely, and the central bank will likely discuss an additional increase in March 2027, when inflation is expected to accelerate into the 3% range," said Takeshi Minami, an economist at Norinchukin Research Institute.

Across the planet, minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve's October meeting released Wednesday also showed that nearly all policymakers expect higher interest rates would be needed to lower inflation.

The minutes "showed strong alignment from Fed officials on the need for additional rate hikes," said MUFG analysts. Markets recently priced a 93% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month.

Many also expect the European Central Bank to raise rates in December, after staying on hold last month, as it is under pressure to address the inflationary backdrop given persistently high energy prices.

A higher interest-rate environment typically diminishes the allure of nonyielding assets such as gold and silver. The hawkish Fed view also likely lifted the dollar, which makes gold and silver--both dollar-denominated commodities--more expensive for investors holding other currencies.

Upcoming U.S. economic data could shape expectations for the size of a December interest rate move by the Fed, said Critical Metals' Tony Sage in a note. This includes the second estimate for the country's third-quarter gross domestic product growth due next week.

"Firm readings could lift yields further and extend gold's losses, while softer prints may offer some relief," he added.

data.title: Moomoo steps up Australian expansion with Sydney Roosters deal, second retail store
data.description:
SYDNEY, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Moomoo Australia and New Zealand today announced its largest local brand investment to date, signing on as platinum partner and official share-trading platform of the Sydney Roosters from the 2027 NRL season.

The deal coincides with the opening of Moomoo's second retail store, in Melbourne's eastern hub of Box Hill, marking one year since the brokerage opened its first physical site in Chatswood, Sydney.

Together, the moves cap four years of rapid local growth, signalling a broader push into mainstream retail and high-net-worth investing. Named Australia's most-trusted investing app in Finder's 2026 customer satisfaction awards, moomoo has also held the top spot as the nation's most-downloaded share-trading app for two consecutive years.*

Sydney Roosters partnership

From the 2027 season, the moomoo logo will appear on the sternum of the Roosters' NRL jersey and the front of their playing shorts, supported by match-day and community activations across Sydney.

"Partnering with a club of the Sydney Roosters' calibre reflects our long-term commitment to the Australian market," said Moomoo Australia and New Zealand chief executive officer Michael McCarthy. "Combining tier-one sporting visibility with face-to-face support in our stores helps build the familiarity and trust everyday Australians want before putting their money to work."

Easts Group chief executive officer Joe Kelly welcomed the announcement. "We’re delighted to welcome moomoo to the Sydney Roosters as our platinum partner and official share-trading platform," he said. "Moomoo is an ambitious, forward-thinking brand with a clear vision for its future. We see a strong alignment between its ambitions and the Roosters’ commitment to performance."

An expanding presence

Since launching locally in 2022, Moomoo Australia and New Zealand has steadily expanded its physical and market presence. Alongside the new Box Hill store and further outlets planned for 2027, the brokerage recently launched Moomoo Priority for high-net-worth users and hosted its inaugural Australian investor day in partnership with Nasdaq. Across Australia and New Zealand the firm’s local headcount will reach 70 staff by the end of 2026.

About moomoo

Moomoo Securities Australia Ltd, a Sydney-based, wholly owned subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed Futu Holdings Ltd, operates the moomoo platform across Australia and New Zealand. The moomoo app gives users access to more than 10,000 shares and exchange-traded funds across the Australian, US and Hong Kong sharemarkets, with US brokerage starting from US99¢ per trade, 24 hours every trading day. The platform pairs low-cost execution with real-time Level 2 US market data, advanced charting, an AI-powered assistant, curated financial news and user forums.

*Source: Sensor Tower, brokerage app downloads in Australia from January 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. Combined total downloads for the moomoo app on Australian iOS and Android stores (referring to the moomoo global app from January 1, 2025 to November 7, 2025, and the Moomoo Australia app from November 7, 2025 onwards). Ranking may change over time.

data.title: AI Selloff Spreads From Wall Street To Asia Despite Anthropic Debut: SPY, QQQ, DIA, Asian Stocks Head For Steep Weekly Losses
data.description:
Key points:
  • Choppy technology trades amid Anthropic’s much-anticipated IPO suppressed liquidity across the board as investors freed up capital to invest in the new AI company on the block.
  • The Taiex in Taiwan plunged nearly 6%, putting the benchmark on course for its worst week since 1991.
  • According to Rajat Agarwal, an Asia equity strategist with Societe Generale, the sharp selloff across the AI sector reflects worries that AI-led growth is slowing down and the “peak growth phase” may have passed.

Global stock markets are headed for a steep red close this week despite Claude-maker Anthropic’s (ANT) record debut on the Nasdaq.

While ANT stock jumped more than 17% on its listing on Thursday, the rest of the U.S. markets took a beating, adding pressure to an already challenging week across the board.

Asian markets, including China, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, also slumped on fears of the unsustainability of the AI boom, and inflation concerns spread far and wide.

US Markets Vs Asia Markets

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100, are poised to end the week more than 5% lower, while the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) is headed for a decline over 6% this week.

Choppy technology trades amid Anthropic’s much-anticipated IPO suppressed liquidity across the board as investors freed up capital to invest in the new AI company on the block. Even Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) strong third-quarter results failed to boost sentiment.

Much like Wall Street, Asia’s main bourses also witnessed a bloodbath, slumping severely at the open on Friday. Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 and Seoul’s KOSPI each plunged about 4.5% in the morning trading. The Taiex in Taiwan plunged nearly 6%, putting the benchmark on course for its worst week since 1991.

The iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF (EWT) has been hit the worst this week, losing nearly 14% so far. The iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY) is also down nearly 6% as the heavily AI-weighted market witnessed a steep selloff in SK Hynix and Samsung, following the AI rout in the U.S.

Meanwhile, the iShares MSCI China ETF (MCHI), and the iShares MSCI Japan ETF (EWJ) are also headed more than 5% lower this week.

Tech Stocks Have Plunged This Week

Among major tech stocks, U.S.-listed shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) have tumbled nearly 12% this week, while American shares of SK Hynix Inc. (SKHY) have lost more than 9.5% of their value so far.

Samsung, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) and NVDA shares have also taken a beating amid the tech rout.

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) is down 10.43%. This is despite the exchange-traded fund drawing more than $13.1 billion year-to-date, on track for its largest annual intake on record, as per The Kobeissi Letter. This month alone, SMH has attracted +$2.2 billion, putting the fund on track for its largest monthly inflow since the +$3.2 billion recorded in July.

Meanwhile, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) is down about 10% this week. As per The Kobeissi Letter, U.S. technology stock valuations have hit their lowest level since March 2020 amid the market correction.

Anthropic’s Record IPO Crunches Liquidity

Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday much above its allocation price of $83. ANT stock soared more than 17% at close, ending the session at $97.17 and taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion.

“The listing of Anthropic failing to lift the market sentiment is the main hit on AI across Asia,” Steven Leung, executive director at UOB Kay Hian Hong Kong Ltd. told Bloomberg.

“Short sellers are seeing no improvement in downside pressure, so there no rush to cover their short positions,” Leung added.

Is AI Trade Running Out Of Growth Catalysts?

According to Rajat Agarwal, an Asia equity strategist with Societe Generale, the sharp selloff across the AI sector reflects worries that AI-led growth is slowing down and the “peak growth phase” may have passed. “The second element is on the demand vacuum that we are seeing,” Agarwal told Al Jazeera.

“At the time when foreigners are not buying, it is to be seen how long can the domestic investors stay put, particularly in Korea, on which the drawdown has been more severe,” he added.

Meanwhile, analyst Michaël van de Poppe said in a post on X that ANT stock would eventually see a selloff after its run-up in the first few days, after which liquidity would rotate toward other risk-on assets.

“I would expect to see $NQ, $BTC and other assets to rally upwards from that liquidity injection alongside a drop in Oil and the Yields,” he said.

Retail Stance: US Vs Asia Markets

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around SPY slipped from ‘bullish’ to ‘neutral’ at the time of writing, while it was ‘bullish’ for QQQ. Sentiment around DIA slipped to ‘bearish’ territory.

Meanwhile, retail sentiment around EWJ was ‘bullish,’ while it was ‘neutral’ for MCHI and EWY. Sentiment around EWT was ‘bearish’ at the time of writing.

data.title: Neugebauer: Texas Court Ruling on Fermi's 70/30 Boardroom Maneuver Is a Loss for 100% of Texas Shareholders
data.description:
• Neugebauer: Under this ruling, the board can entrench itself with one quick vote, while shareholders need 70% of all outstanding shares to fight back.
  • Neugebauer: "That isn't Texas-style good governance. It's entrenchment."
  • Directors who failed to win a majority on October 30 are still sitting in the boardroom.
  • Neugebauer filing appeal because Texas's standing as the best place to do business in America depends on getting this right.
  • Texan voters have made it clear that they don't accept that people in power can do whatever they want and change the rules whenever it suits them.

DALLAS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Toby Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc. (d/b/a Fermi America) (Nasdaq: FRMI) ("Fermi" or the "Company"), today issued the following statement after the Texas Business Court dismissed his claims in Neugebauer v. Fermi Inc. challenging the 70% supermajority bylaw the Company's board adopted in May without a shareholder vote.

"This isn't just a loss for Melissa and me. I believe it's a loss for every shareholder of every Texas company," said Toby Neugebauer. "Under this ruling, a board can change the rules in the middle of a fight, without a shareholder vote. It takes the board one quick vote to change the rules. It takes shareholders 70% of all outstanding shares to have a voice. Do the math. A little over 30% can block anything, and a share that is never voted counts as a no.

"Directors who could not win a majority of the shareholder support are still sitting in the boardroom. I don't think that is Texas-style good governance. It's entrenchment."

On May 13, 2026, in the middle of a shareholder contest, Fermi's board amended the Company's bylaws. Under the amendment, shareholders now need 70% of all outstanding shares to expand the board or change how the bylaws are amended. The board, however, can change those same rules with a simple majority vote of its directors. In August, the board changed director elections to require a majority of all outstanding shares, with unvoted shares counting as a no vote. At the October 30 annual meeting, neither director on the ballot reached that majority. Both men remain on the board.

"I'm proud of the work Texas has done to become the best place in America to do business," Neugebauer continued. "But capital flows to boards that answer to their owners. If shareholders can be silenced whenever a board disagrees with them, investors will notice."

This November, voters rejected the insider, pay-to-play politics that has harmed Fermi. Texans have made it clear that they don't accept that people in power can do whatever they want and change the rules whenever it suits them. We respectfully disagree with the Court and feel confident that we will be successful on appeal, because this isn't how good governance works.

Texas earned its business reputation. Now it has to protect it. I will continue to advocate for good governance, not for financial gain, but for the good of Texas.

data.title: Treasury rally spills over to Indian bonds, debt supply slows move
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

Indian government bonds were marginally higher in early deals on Friday, tracking a rise in US Treasuries, while the major focus shifted to fresh supply through the weekly debt auction, with the cutoffs set to drive the markets later in the day.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield was at 7.2439% as of 10 a.m. IST, after closing at 7.2543% on Thursday.

New Delhi will sell bonds worth 330 billion rupees ($3.54 billion), including the liquid five-year paper.

"Bulls are trying their best to drag yields further down, but some profit-taking and caution before the auction is not allowing any major rally," trader with a primary dealership said.

"The real direction will probably emerge later, once the cutoff is known."

US Treasury yields eased on Thursday as a sharp selloff in US equities prompted investors to move into safe-haven government bonds.

The decline in yields also comes against a softer economic backdrop and traders are increasingly pricing in the possibility that the Federal Reserve will take a more measured approach at its December meeting.

According to CME FedWatch data, the probability of a 50-basis-point hike has dropped to about 3%, after briefly rising as high as 14% earlier in the week.

The benchmark Brent crude remains around $92 a barrel, but oil prices continue to be highly sensitive to developments around the Strait of Hormuz, and any prolonged disruption in the region could rapidly tighten global supplies.

For India, higher oil prices remain a key macroeconomic risk, as it impacts the nation's current account deficit, local currency and inflation trajectory.

Markets have therefore positioned for the Reserve Bank of India to potentially deliver another rate increase in early December, after India's retail inflation moved above the 6% upper tolerance threshold for the first time in two years.

RATES

Overnight index swap rates were down, but trading volumes remained thing.

The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate was at 6.46%, while the two-year rate (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) was not yet traded. The more liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate was at 6.48%.

($1 = 93.2900 Indian rupees)
